This work establishes a biodegradable therapeutic-monitoring bioelectronic platform and advances peripheral nerve repair from passive conductive scaffolds toward intelligent implantable bioelectronics.

papers.title: Resting-State EEG Aperiodic Activity and Negative Affective Vulnerability: The Mediating Role of Big Five Personality Traits.
papers.abstract: Resting-state EEG aperiodic parameters characterize the broadband background component of neural activity. The offset reflects overall broadband power and has been linked to population-level firing, whereas the exponent is often interpreted, within a theoretical framework, as an indirect proxy for cortical excitation/inhibition (E/I) balance. These measures may therefore provide candidate neurophysiological trait markers of negative affective vulnerability, but it remains unclear whether their associations with trait anxiety and trait depression are direct or are statistically accounted for by stable personality traits. A total of 164 healthy adults completed measures of the Big Five personality traits, trait anxiety, and trait depression and underwent eyes-closed resting-state EEG recording. Aperiodic exponent and offset were estimated at the whole-brain and regional levels using spectral parameterization. Partial correlations, hierarchical regression analyses, and bootstrap mediation analyses were conducted controlling for sex, age, and years of education. Neuroticism showed the strongest and most spatially widespread positive associations with the aperiodic exponent. Trait anxiety showed more limited associations, mainly with whole-brain and frontal aperiodic parameters. The association between whole-brain exponent and trait anxiety was no longer significant after the Big Five personality traits were entered into the model. Bootstrap mediation analyses identified significant indirect effects in this association through personality traits, with neuroticism showing the largest indirect effect and conscientiousness also showing a significant indirect effect. Trait depression was not directly associated with aperiodic parameters, although significant indirect effects through personality traits were observed. Resting-state EEG aperiodic activity, particularly the exponent, was more consistently associated with stable personality dispositions than with negative affective vulnerability directly. Personality traits, especially neuroticism, may statistically account for part of the association between aperiodic exponent and trait anxiety. Because the data were cross-sectional, the temporal and causal direction of these associations cannot be determined.

papers.title: Persistent pocket-site pain after cardiac implantable electronic device implantation: a prospective observational study of prevalence, neuropathic characteristics, and quality of life.
papers.abstract: Although transvenous cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) implantation is generally considered a minor procedure, long-lasting pocket-site pain may represent an underrecognized clinical problem. This study aimed to evaluate the prevalence, characteristics, and clinical impact of persistent pain after CIED implantation. This prospective observational study included patients who underwent first-time CIED implantation and attended routine outpatient follow-up visits. Pain intensity was assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), and neuropathic pain characteristics were evaluated using the Douleur Neuropathique 4 Questions (DN-4) questionnaire. Health-related quality of life was assessed using the Short Form-12 (SF-12). Demographic and clinical data were also recorded. A total of 102 patients were included in the analysis. Persistent implantation-site pain (VAS ≥ 4) was reported by 22.5% of patients. Neuropathic pain characteristics (DN-4 ≥ 4) were identified in 26.5% of patients. A moderate positive correlation was observed between VAS and DN-4 scores (ρ = 0.473, p < 0.001). However, the association between VAS ≥ 4 and DN-4 ≥ 4 was not statistically significant and had a small effect size (p = 0.118; φ = 0.15). Pain intensity was moderately negatively correlated with the SF-12 physical component score, indicating reduced physical quality of life with increasing pain severity, while mental quality of life was not significantly affected. Persistent pocket-site pain after CIED implantation affected a clinically meaningful proportion of patients despite generally low overall pain scores. Higher DN-4 scores were associated with poorer physical and mental quality of life and may provide additional clinical information in selected patients. However, because the categorical association between VAS-defined persistent pain and DN-4 positivity was not statistically significant, these findings should be interpreted cautiously and confirmed in larger prospective studies.

papers.title: Occupational hazards and workplace safety practices among nurses in Nablus, Palestine: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: Hospital nurses encounter physical, ergonomic, biological, chemical, psychological, and social occupational hazards. Although these hazards are widely recognized, a knowledge gap remains in Palestine regarding multidimensional work-related symptoms examined together with selected workplace exposure, prevention, personal protective equipment, and organizational safety practices. An analytical cross-sectional study included 140 registered nurses from medical, surgical, pediatric, and gynecology/obstetrics departments at three hospitals in Nablus, Palestine. The final analytical sample represented 87.5% of the 160 distributed questionnaires. Data were collected using an English-language structured questionnaire comprising demographic and professional characteristics, the Work-Related Symptom Scale (WRSS), and 18 study-specific heterogeneous workplace items. Because the 18 items mixed exposure conditions, preventive behaviors, personal protective equipment, cognitive demands, and organizational practices, they were interpreted primarily at item level rather than as a validated unidimensional scale. Analyses were conducted using IBM SPSS Statistics, Version 19.0; subgroup comparisons were treated as exploratory. Physical symptoms were reported more frequently than psychological and social symptoms. Sleep disturbances were rated present by 37.9% and highly present by 19.3% of participants; corresponding values were 33.6% and 21.4% for leg pain and 31.4% and 20.7% for back pain. Psychological and social symptoms were generally reported at lower perceived levels than physical symptoms, although underreporting cannot be excluded. Among the study-specific workplace items, the highest proportions selecting "always" were observed for hand washing (60.7%), direct contact with patients (56.4%), general safety measures (55.0%), mask use (55.0%), and documented incident reporting (50.7%). In exploratory subgroup analysis, female nurses had a higher mean physical WRSS score than male nurses (3.17 vs. 2.73; mean difference 0.44; p = 0.002). The findings identify a prominent pattern of sleep-related and musculoskeletal symptoms among nurses in the participating Nablus hospitals and heterogeneous responses across workplace exposure, prevention, personal protective equipment, and organizational safety items. These cross-sectional self-reported findings may inform consideration of targeted ergonomic risk assessment, safe-patient-handling support, task-specific personal protective equipment policies, incident-reporting systems, and department-level occupational safety planning. Causal and population-wide inferences should be avoided. Not applicable.

papers.title: The effect of sleep quality and depressive symptoms on the relationship between burnout and health-related productivity loss in nurses working in intensive care: a cross-sectional study from the Chinese nurses' health cohort study (TARGET).
papers.abstract: Burnout is highly prevalent among ICU nurses and compromises physical and psychological well-being, leading to productivity loss. However, limited evidence exists regarding the pathways through which burnout influences productivity, particularly the role of sleep disturbance and depression. Few studies have examined the mechanisms through which burnout affects health-related productivity in intensive care unit (ICU) nurses. This study addresses this gap by investigating the sequential mediating role of sleep quality and depressive symptoms in the relationship between burnout and health-related productivity loss. A cross-sectional study. Baseline data from the Chinese Nurses' Health Cohort Study, collected between December 2020 and February 2024, included 3,491 ICU nurses. Burnout, health-related productivity loss, sleep quality and depressive symptoms were assessed using the Maslach Burnout Inventory-Human Services Survey, Stanford Presenteeism Scale, Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index and Patient Health Questionnaire-9. Chain mediation analysis was conducted using the SPSS PROCESS macro, and subgroup analyses were performed. Data from 3,491 ICU nurses were analyzed. Subgroup analyses showed female nurses aged 18-30 years, with a master's degree or above, senior titles, contract positions, clinical roles, and 6-10 years of experience reported higher productivity loss. Productivity loss correlated with burnout, poor sleep quality, and depressive symptoms. Mediation analysis using Bootstrap resampling (5,000 iterations) revealed that burnout had a significant total effect on productivity loss (β = 0.1019, 95% CI [0.0963, 0.1076]). The direct effect remained significant after accounting for mediators (β = 0.0587, 95% CI [0.0527, 0.0647]). The sequential indirect effect through sleep quality and depressive symptoms was significant (β = 0.0422, 95% CI [0.0395, 0.0469]), indicating that burnout impaired sleep quality, which increased depressive symptoms and ultimately contributed to greater productivity loss. The relationship between burnout and health-related productivity is mediated by sleep quality and depressive symptoms. Interventions reducing burnout, improving sleep quality, and preventing depression may help mitigate productivity loss. The study protocol for TARGET was registered with the China Clinical Trial Registry (registration number: ChiCTR2100043202, February 8, 2021, https://trialsearch.who.int/Default.aspx ).

papers.title: Reduced neural sensitivity to emotional faces and voices in preterm five-year-olds: a comparative study.
papers.abstract: Accurate emotion processing is crucial for social development. Preterm birth is associated with neurodevelopmental alterations and increased vulnerability to subtle socio-emotional difficulties, often described within the preterm behavioral phenotype. Previous studies have reported impaired emotion recognition in preterm populations, but have largely relied on behavioral tasks and primarily focused on facial expressions. Because explicit emotion recognition is still developing in early childhood, objective neural markers of implicit emotion discrimination may be particularly informative for early detection. We administered a series of frequency-tagging electroencephalography (EEG) paradigms to investigate neural sensitivity to brief changes in emotional expressions in a cohort of five-year-old preterm children (N = 66), and age-matched full-term peers (N = 32). Frequency-tagging EEG utilizes fast periodic stimulation to elicit synchronized brain responses measurable in the frequency domain. Neural sensitivity to changes in emotional expressions was examined in both the visual and auditory modality, using oddball paradigms with neutral faces or voices presented at base frequency and emotional expressions (either fearful or happy) presented as periodic oddballs. Linear mixed models were used to investigate the effects of group, emotion, and prematurity severity. All children showed implicit neural discrimination between neutral and emotional expressions. Compared to full-term peers, children born before 32 weeks of gestation, but not those born between 33 and 36 weeks of gestation, showed reduced neural sensitivity to facial emotional expression changes. In contrast, all preterm children (< 37 weeks of gestation) showed reduced neural sensitivity to vocal emotional expression changes. Across modalities, reduced neural sensitivity to happy emotional expressions was associated with higher parent-reported social difficulties. Five-year-old children born preterm show reduced neural sensitivity to brief changes in facial and vocal emotional expressions compared with full-term peers. Strikingly, the impact of prematurity severity differed between the visual and auditory modalities, indicating differential maturation of higher-level visual and auditory processing following preterm birth. These findings contribute to a more detailed understanding of socio-emotional development after preterm birth and highlight the importance of early, modality-sensitive monitoring of socio-emotional development across the entire preterm population.

papers.title: Efficacy of progressive muscle relaxation training in post-traumatic stress disorder after the Kahramanmaraş earthquake: a randomized controlled trial.
papers.abstract: The February 6, 2023 Kahramanmaraş earthquake was one of Turkey's most devastating natural disasters, causing serious psychological issues, especially Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). Although various treatments exist for PTSD, they can be costly and sometimes ineffective. Progressive Muscle Relaxation Training (PMRT) is a low‑cost, self‑administered technique with no side effects, but randomized controlled trials on its effectiveness for post‑earthquake PTSD remain very limited. This randomized trial examined whether PMRT effectively treats PTSD in individuals after the Kahramanmaraş earthquake. The study included 44 earthquake-affected individuals aged 18-65 who met at least one of the following criteria: formal DSM-5 PTSD diagnosis by a psychiatrist, or a PCL-5 score of 47 or higher (indicating clinically significant PTSD symptoms). Based on power analysis, 22 participants were assigned to each group via block randomization: PMRT and control. All received PTSD and healthy lifestyle information; those on ongoing treatment continued. The PMRT group additionally received 6 weeks (twice/week, 20-30 min/session) of telerehabilitation-based PMRT. Assessments (PCL-5, DASS-21, PSQI, FSS, SF-36) were conducted pre- and post-intervention. Time-group interactions were analyzed with two-way mixed ANOVA (p < 0.05). In the PMRT group, PTSD symptom severity significantly decreased after the intervention (p < 0.001; η²p = 0.735). Significant improvements were also observed in depression (η²p = 0.435), anxiety (η²p = 0.521), stress (η²p = 0.504), sleep quality (η²p = 0.632), fatigue (η²p = 0.477), and both physical (η²p = 0.727) and mental (η²p = 0.630) components of quality of life compared to the control group (p < 0.001). In the control group, no significant changes were observed in these parameters, while sleep quality and physical health deteriorated in the control group. PMRT was associated with greater improvements in PTSD symptoms, psychological well-being, sleep quality, fatigue, and quality of life compared to an education-only control group. Telerehabilitation may offer a practical advantage when face-to-face care is limited, although this remains speculative. NCT07164261-02.09.2025.

papers.title: Sleep disorders as an emerging risk factor for liver cirrhosis and hepatocellular carcinoma: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies.
papers.abstract: Sleep disorders are increasingly recognized as contributors to metabolic dysfunction and chronic liver disease, but their associations with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and cirrhosis remain unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis to evaluate the relationship between sleep disorders and liver-related outcomes. Following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420261342781), we searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library through February 2026 for cohort studies assessing sleep disorders and liver outcomes. Adjusted hazard ratios (HRs) or odds ratios (ORs) were pooled using random-effects models. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed, and risk of bias was assessed using ROBINS-I. Thirteen cohort studies were included. Overall, sleep disorders were associated with an increased risk of liver-related outcomes (HR 1.49; 95% CI 1.22-1.81; I² = 96%). Insomnia was significantly associated with increased risk (HR 1.39; 95% CI 1.28-1.49), whereas obstructive sleep apnea showed a non-significant trend (HR 1.80; 95% CI 0.91-3.58). Sleep disorders were linked to higher risks of HCC (HR 1.42; 95% CI 1.15-1.77) and unspecified liver cancer (HR 1.26; 95% CI 1.01-1.57), but not cirrhosis. Findings were robust in sensitivity analyses, with no significant publication bias. Sleep disorders, particularly insomnia, are associated with increased risks of HCC and liver-related outcomes. These findings highlight sleep disturbances as potentially modifiable risk factors in liver disease progression.

papers.title: Epilepsy in paediatric neurofibromatosis type 1: clinical features and associated factors in a single-centere cohort.
papers.abstract: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1) is associated with an increased risk of epilepsy, but the clinical spectrum and associated factors of epilepsy in paediatric NF1 remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to describe frequency and features of epilepsy in paediatric NF1 and to compare the characteristics of NF1 patients with and without epilepsy. We retrospectively reviewed 253 paediatric NF1 patients followed up between January 2020 and December 2025. Demographic, clinical, electroencephalographic, and radiological data were collected. Categorical comparisons between patients with and without epilepsy were performed using χ2 or Fisher's exact tests. Of 253 patients (53.8% female; median age 12.3 years), 12 (4.74%) had epilepsy. Median age at epilepsy onset was 3.2 years (IQR 2.4-7.0). Seizure semiology was focal in 7 (58.3%) and generalized in 5 (41.7%). EEG reports were available in 10 patients: normal in 4, focal discharges in 4, and multifocal discharges in 2; no patient had generalized spike-and-wave discharges. Four (33.3%) had drug-resistant epilepsy; median number of antiseizure medications was 1, median seizure-free duration was 44 months. Compared with patients without epilepsy, those with epilepsy had significantly higher rates of moyamoya syndrome (25.0% vs 0.4%, p < 0.001), autism spectrum disorder (16.7% vs 0%, p = 0.002), learning difficulties (58.3% vs 14.5%, p < 0.001), and overall neurodevelopmental comorbidity (83.3% vs 29.0%, p < 0.001). No significant differences were found in the frequencies of neurofibromatosis bright objects (NBOs), optic pathway gliomas, or low-grade gliomas. In our cohort, epilepsy occurred in 4.74% of patients. Most had favorable seizure outcomes. Epilepsy was associated with cerebrovascular anomalies and neurodevelopmental comorbidities but not with NBOs or intracranial tumours. These findings suggest that children with NF1 and cerebrovascular abnormalities may warrant particular vigilance for seizures, while those with epilepsy should undergo systematic neurodevelopmental assessment. • Epilepsy affects 4-14% of patients with NF1, is usually mild, but its determinants remain poorly defined. • Neurofibromatosis bright objects show no consistent association with epilepsy. • In 253 children, epilepsy (4.74%) was associated with moyamoya syndrome and neurodevelopmental comorbidity. • Optic pathway gliomas, low-grade gliomas and bright objects did not predict epilepsy.

papers.title: SOFEx: A Self-Organized Feature Extraction Approach for Detecting Mild Cognitive Impairment and Alzheimer's Disease using EEG Datasets.
papers.abstract: Early differentiation of mild cognitive impairment (MCI) from Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains difficult because diagnosis integrates cognitive, imaging, laboratory, and neurological evidence. EEG-based models may provide complementary information, but fixed descriptors can miss signal-specific structure. SOFEx was developed as an adaptive and interpretable EEG feature-engineering framework. The analysis used 1,905 EEG segments from 451 recordings of 168 participants (59 AD, seven MCI, and 102 controls). SOFEx combined self-organized rose pattern extraction, fold-wise feature selection, channel-wise classification, and iterative majority voting. Validation used leave-one-subject-out (LOSO), leave-one-record-out (LORO), and participant-grouped 10-fold cross-validation (CV). Five classifiers were compared under LOSO, and a support vector machine (SVM) was retained. LOSO, used as the primary evaluation of generalization to unseen participants, achieved 84.09% accuracy (95% Wilson CI, 82.38-85.67%), with class-wise recall of 94.47% for AD, 56.59% for controls, and 21.18% for MCI (UAR, 57.41%; macro F1-score, 62.95%). LORO and participant-grouped 10-fold CV achieved 93.65% and 96.38% accuracy, respectively, indicating substantial performance variation across validation schemes. Frontal and parietal electrodes contributed repeatedly to the selected configurations, providing sensor-space information on the signals supporting classification. SOFEx provides an adaptive and interpretable feature-engineering framework for EEG-based classification, combining input-specific pattern selection with sensor-level traceability. Participant-independent evaluation showed high sensitivity for AD, while discrimination of MCI remained more challenging. These findings support the potential of the proposed framework and motivate further validation on larger and independent cohorts to assess its generalizability across clinical settings.

papers.title: Response to comment on: the association between obstructive sleep apnoea and erectile dysfunction: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Functional architecture of the human insula.
papers.abstract: The insular cortex has a central role in pain1,2, interoception3,4 and feelings5,6, yet its functional architecture and causal electrophysiological relationships among its subregions remain poorly understood. Here we combine intracranial electrical stimulation and task-based electroencephalography recordings with connectivity mapping within a cytoarchitectonic atlas of the human insula7-10 in 87 participants implanted with intracranial electrodes, and identify a quadripartite functional architecture comprising four distinct regions: (1) a dorsal-posterior region encoding somatotopically organized nociceptive/thermoceptive and somatosensory signals; (2) a ventral-posterior region with access to somatic information across multiple body parts; (3) a mid-anterior region associated with visceral sensations and anxiety states; and (4) an anterior-polar region, largely silent to direct stimulation, yet showing robust activation during salience detection and change of action mode. Critically, this anterior region, with its strong connections with the prefrontal cortex, including the anterior cingulate cortex, exerts strong and direct influence over other insular regions, while receiving less-strong indirect inputs from them, revealing an electrophysiological pathway for cognitive modulation of pain and bodily perception. Together, these findings define a functional architecture of the human insula that links cytoarchitecture to directed and asymmetric electrophysiological interactions, with mechanistic implications for cognitive modulation of pain and interoceptive experience.

papers.title: SIK3 controls synaptic localization of NMDA receptors by phosphorylating GluN1.
papers.abstract: Synaptic NMDA-type glutamate receptors (NMDARs) are central components of all neural computations. NMDAR levels critically vary between synapses but how the synaptic localization of NMDARs is controlled remains unclear. Here we show that SIK3, a serine-threonine protein kinase, localizes to synapses where it phosphorylates the obligatory NMDAR subunit GluN1 at a single site. This single phosphorylation event controls NMDAR recruitment to synapses. Genetic deletion of SIK3 severely and selectively decreases synaptic GluN1 levels by ~60% without altering AMPA-type glutamate receptor levels or inducing major transcriptional changes. Pharmacological inhibition of SIK3 impairs synaptic NMDAR responses within 45 minutes. Mutating the SIK3-phosphorylation site inhibits GluN1 synaptic recruitment. 'Sleepy', a gain-of-function mutation in SIK3 that increases sleep, selectively enhances synaptic NMDAR levels by increasing GluN1 phosphorylation. Thus, SIK3 phosphorylation of GluN1 provides a key signal for recruiting NMDARs to synapses.

papers.title: A corticohypothalamic circuit that mediates maternal awakening to pup cries.
papers.abstract: Maternal caregiving requires sensory vigilance to ensure offspring survival, particularly during sleep. Infant cries are salient sensory cues that reliably trigger maternal arousal and caregiving responses in both humans and dams, but the underlying neural circuitry remains poorly defined. Here we identify a corticohypothalamic circuit in mice that mediates maternal awakening in response to pup calls. We show that layer 6 (L6) neurons in the temporal association cortex and ectorhinal cortex (TeA/Ect) projecting to the preoptic area (POA) exhibit enhanced responsiveness to pup calls after the transition to motherhood. This enhanced responsiveness is mediated by increased expression of dopamine receptor D1 (Drd1) in TeA/Ect → POA neurons. Additionally, we reveal a pathway from the auditory thalamus to L6 TeA/Ect neurons that transmits pup cues during sleep. Together, these findings identify a dedicated neural circuit that grants infant cries privileged access to arousal systems, likely representing a fundamental adaptation for caregiving across mammals.

papers.title: Long-range interdependencies aware signal analysis for rapid and accurate obstructive sleep apnea prediction.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea, characterized by frequent interruptions in breathing and intermittent hypoxia, is a public health concern due to its potential to increase multiple organ system morbidity and mortality. Although polysomnography is the gold standard for diagnosis, it is laborious, costly, and complex. Here, we present a biological geometry-aware artificial intelligence framework that processes physiological signals to predict sleep apnea severity. This framework extracts multifractal coupling features that capture long-range dependencies among physiological processes and integrates them into deep learning for classification. We validate this approach across five heterogeneous cohorts comprising more than 35,000 subjects. The method achieves robust and consistent performance, with area-under-the-curve values exceeding 0.91 and improvements of 8-18% over state-of-the-art models. The extracted coupling representations exhibit rapid convergence and consistent performance across heterogeneous cohorts. This framework provides a robust representation of physiological dynamics and supports future developments in automated analysis of sleep-disordered breathing.

papers.title: Patients' perceptions of hypnotic medications and factors associated with the desire to discontinue among regular users: A cross-sectional questionnaire survey in community pharmacies.
papers.abstract: Long-term use of hypnotic medications is associated with adverse events, and clinical guidelines recommend periodic reassessment and deprescribing when appropriate. However, little is known about patients who perceive hypnotic medications as necessary while wishing to discontinue treatment. This study investigated the association between perceived necessity and the desire to discontinue treatment and factors associated with discontinuation desire among patients who perceived hypnotics as necessary. A cross-sectional anonymous questionnaire survey was conducted among patients receiving regular hypnotic therapy at community pharmacies in June 2026. The questionnaire assessed perceived necessity, desire to discontinue, concerns about adverse effects, sleep quality, and treatment satisfaction. The association between perceived necessity and discontinuation desire was evaluated using the chi-square test. Factors associated with discontinuation desire among patients who perceived hypnotics as necessary were examined using multivariable logistic regression. Among 193 patients, 163 (84.5%) perceived hypnotic medications as necessary every day; of these, 56 (34.4%) wished to discontinue treatment. In contrast, 19 of 30 patients (63.3%) who did not perceive hypnotic medications as necessary every day expressed a desire to discontinue treatment (p = 0.003). Among patients perceiving hypnotics as necessary, concerns about adverse effects were associated with discontinuation desire (odds ratio, 4.01; 95% confidence interval, 1.92-8.38; p < 0.001). These exploratory findings demonstrate that perceived necessity and discontinuation desire can coexist and warrant prospective investigation of patients' perceptions and subsequent deprescribing behavior.

papers.title: Advances in neurological disease models and optimization of the laboratory animal environment for reproducible research.
papers.abstract: Animal models of neurological diseases have evolved from phenotype-based systems to integrated platforms that link genetics, molecular signaling, synaptic physiology, neural circuits, behavior, and therapeutic responses. Simultaneously, increasingly precise phenotyping has revealed that experimental outcomes are strongly influenced by age, microbiological status, diet, housing, stress, previous experience, health status, and measurement methodology. This review considers these two developments to be complementary requirements for reliable experimental neuroscience. Studies on voltage-gated calcium channel mutants have shown that defined genetic alterations can produce age-dependent abnormalities in motor function, cognition, emotion, autonomic regulation, and seizure susceptibility. Studies on N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptor-Calcium-calmodulin-dependent protein kinase II (CaMKII) signaling, epigenetic regulators, stress-related phenotypes, and fear memory circuits have further illustrated how animal models can be characterized across levels, from molecular mechanisms to neural ensembles and therapeutic rescues. Translation to common marmosets extends these approaches to primate sleep and epilepsy, while highlighting the effects of genetic diversity, spontaneous disease, handling, and colony management. In parallel, studies on germ-free animals, diet, the gut microbiota, barrier facilities, cage enrichment, telemetry, and veterinary monitoring have demonstrated that husbandry variables, rather than technical background, are biological determinants. Integrating rigorous disease model characterization with evidence-based husbandry, environmental control, and transparent reporting should improve the reproducibility and translational value of preclinical neuroscience research and the welfare of the animals used.

papers.title: Living in a shared room is associated with worse pain and sleep during hospital admission after arthroscopic rotator cuff repair.
papers.abstract: To investigate whether hospital room type is associated with postoperative sleep quality and pain levels during the acute inpatient period in patients undergoing arthroscopic rotator cuff repair. A prospective cohort study was conducted from November 2021 to December 2023, including 127 patients (mean age, 61.3 ± 8.3 years) who underwent arthroscopic rotator cuff repair. Patients were allocated to single-bed (n = 15), double-bed (n = 42), or multi-bed rooms (n = 70). Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and pain was evaluated using visual analogue scale (VAS) scores. Pre- and postoperative comparisons within groups were performed using matched-pair analyses, and Kruskal-Wallis tests were used for comparisons across groups. Postoperative PSQI scores increased significantly from baseline in the double-bed (6.2 ± 3 to 7.2 ± 2; p = 0.003) and multi-bed groups (5.4 ± 3 to 6.9 ± 3; p < 0.001), whereas no significant change was observed in the single-bed group (4.7 ± 4 to 6.1 ± 4; p = 0.528). Similarly, VAS scores increased in the double-bed (1.46 ± 1 to 2.07 ± 1; p = 0.003) and multi-bed groups (1.40 ± 1 to 1.94 ± 1; p < 0.001), but remained stable in the single-bed group (p = 0.366). Patients accommodated in shared rooms experienced greater deterioration in sleep quality and higher pain levels following arthroscopic rotator cuff repair compared to those in single-bed rooms. These findings suggest that hospital room type may influence early postoperative recovery.
papers.journal: Journal of the Formosan Medical Association = Taiwan yi zhi

papers.title: [Digital phenotyping in psychiatry: Concepts, systems, and clinical implications].
papers.abstract: Digital phenotyping uses smartphones, wearable devices, and embedded sensors to repeatedly quantify behavioral and physiological features in real-world settings. Its development in psychiatry raises conceptual, methodological, clinical, infrastructural, and ethical questions. This scoping review aimed to map the different understandings of digital phenotyping, their applications, and their main limitations. A scoping review was conducted. PubMed was searched for publications issued between January 1st, 2015, and December 31st, 2025. Publications directly addressing the conceptual foundations, methodologies, infrastructures, clinical applications, or ethical implications of digital phenotyping in psychiatry and mental health were eligible. The included publications were synthesized using thematic analysis. Forty-five publications were included and classified into five thematic domains: epistemology and epistemic injustice; clinical reasoning and decision models; sociotechnical systems and infrastructures; ethical considerations; and computational models and data-driven frameworks. Digital phenotyping enables the longitudinal assessment of mobility, sleep, activity, sociability, smartphone use, and selected physiological parameters. However, the resulting signals are shaped by device characteristics, sampling strategies, preprocessing decisions, and analytical models. Methodological heterogeneity, limited external validation, platform dependency, and unresolved issues concerning clinical integration and data governance currently restrict generalizability. Digital phenotyping may complement clinical interviews and improve the study of individual trajectories, but it does not provide an exhaustive representation of mental states or constitute a validated biomarker in itself. Its clinical value depends on methodological reproducibility, robust infrastructures, demonstrable decision-making utility, and contextual interpretation by clinicians.

papers.title: Is napping harmless? Nighttime sleep health and all-cause mortality in community-dwelling older Vietnamese adults.
papers.abstract: This study examined whether nap types (duration and regular vs. as-needed naps) were associated with mortality among older Vietnamese adults and whether nighttime sleep health moderated this association. Data were from the Longitudinal Study of Ageing and Health in Vietnam (2018-2023; n=4447; baseline mean age=69.74 years; 55.5% female). All-cause mortality at 4-year follow-up was the outcome. Self-reported napping included no nap (reference), regular short naps (<30 minutes), regular intermediate naps (30-59minutes), regular long naps (≥60 minutes), as-needed short naps, as-needed intermediate naps, and as-needed long naps. Poor nighttime sleep health was conceptualized using 4 SATED dimensions (sleep dissatisfaction, daytime sleepiness, sleep discontinuity, and suboptimal sleep duration). At baseline, two-thirds of respondents took naps regularly or as-needed. There were 514 deaths at follow-up (12%). Adjusted logistic regression analysis showed that only regular long naps were associated with elevated death risk, adjusting for nighttime sleep health and covariates (OR=1.39, 95% CI=1.05-1.86). Early-mortality odds did not differ significantly between the other nap types and non-nappers. The interaction between as-needed long naps and poor nighttime sleep health was related to mortality (OR=1.32, 95% CI=1.01-1.72). The adjusted probability of death increased significantly with poorer nighttime sleep health for all nap types, except for regular long naps (which remained high regardless of nighttime sleep health) and regular short naps (which declined with poorer nighttime sleep health scores). Despite the nap culture, taking long naps regularly was associated with higher mortality risks among older Vietnamese. Besides, the link between napping and mortality may be influenced by nighttime sleep health.

papers.title: Depression in the prodromal phase of Parkinson's disease: Clinical manifestations, biomarker evidence, and predictive implications.
papers.abstract: Depression is one of the earliest and most frequent non-motor symptoms in the prodromal phase of Parkinson's disease (PD), often preceding motor signs by years to decades. This review synthesizes epidemiological, neuroimaging, biomarker, and genetic evidence to clarify whether depression is a risk factor, a direct prodromal manifestation, or both. Meta-analyses consistently show a two-fold increased risk of subsequent PD in individuals with depressive symptoms or major depressive disorder (MDD), with the highest risk occurring within 1-2 years of diagnosis but persisting for up to 25 years. Late-onset depressive syndrome (after age 50-60) is associated with dopaminergic deficits on dopamine transporter imaging in 24-79% of cases, supporting it as a prodromal symptom, whereas early-onset depression may act through shared genetic vulnerability or chronic inflammatory pathways. Neuroimaging in isolated REM sleep behavior disorder (iRBD) reveals that depression correlates with caudate atrophy, frontostriatal white matter disruption, and brainstem monoaminergic dysfunction, but not simply with nigrostriatal denervation. Depression frequently coexists with RBD, autonomic dysfunction, and olfactory impairment, likely reflecting shared brainstem pathology. Genetic forms of PD (GBA1, SNCA, LRRK2, PRKN) show variable depression prevalence, providing mechanistic insights into lysosomal, inflammatory, and proteostatic pathways. Emerging evidence implicates IL-17A, sIL-2R, and α-synuclein (α-syn) aggregation as convergent points linking depression and prodromal α-synucleinopathy, with gut-brain axis dysfunction potentially amplifying this process. Current Movement Disorder Society prodromal PD criteria include depression but have limited sensitivity in general populations. No disease-modifying trials have tested whether treating prodromal depression alters phenoconversion risk. We conclude that proximal, late-onset depressive syndrome is a robust prodromal marker, while distant or early-onset depression, including MDD, identifies a chronically elevated risk population. Future studies should integrate multimodal biomarkers and test therapeutic interventions in prodromal cohorts.

papers.title: [Strategies for perioperative pain management and the prevention and management of postoperative delirium in frail older patients].
papers.abstract: Postoperative pain and postoperative delirium (POD) may share some pathophysiological mechanisms in frail older patients. Persistent nociceptive input, accumulation of analgesic drugs, hemodynamic fluctuations, and respiratory depression may increase the risk of acute brain dysfunction. Potential mechanisms include blood-brain barrier disruption and neuroinflammation, disturbances in cerebral perfusion and oxygen metabolism, and disruption of sleep and arousal networks. A systematic review suggests a dose-response relationship between postoperative pain intensity and POD, although the certainty of the evidence is low and causality remains unproven. This article proposes a "dual-exposure, three-pathway, closed-loop management" framework for perioperative analgesia and the prevention and management of postoperative delirium in frail older patients. Preoperative assessment should include frailty, cognitive status, and pain-related risk. Intraoperatively, precision multimodal analgesia should be tailored to incisional, visceral, and inflammatory pain, with the regimen adjusted using data from nociception, electroencephalographic, cerebral oxygenation, and hemodynamic monitoring. Postoperatively, pain should be assessed repeatedly over time, together with concurrent screening for POD and identification of reversible precipitating factors. The goal of analgesia in frail older patients should not be defined simply as "zero pain" or complete avoidance of opioids. Instead, adequate analgesia should be provided while minimizing treatment-related adverse effects that may impair brain function.

papers.title: [Research progress in chrono-nutrition for four major chronic and non-communicable diseases].
papers.abstract: Chronic and non-communicable disease is the leading cause of death and disease burden globally. Traditional prevention and control strategies mainly focuses on dietary composition and total energy intake, with less emphasis on the temporal patterns of eating behavior. Chrono-nutrition, as an emerging interdisciplinary field, focuses on the interaction between meal timing, frequency, regularity, and the body's endogenous circadian rhythms, and its impact on health. This paper systematically summarizes the influence and potential mechanisms of chrono-nutrition in four major chronic and non-communicable diseases: cardiovascular disease, cancer, diabetes, and chronic respiratory disease. Current evidence indicates that irregular meal time (e.g., skipping breakfast, postponed evening meal, or eating at nighttime), prolonged eating windows, and disordered eating frequency might be associated with an increased risk or poor prognosis of cardiovascular disease, cancer, and type Ⅱ diabetes. The underlying mechanisms involve lipid metabolism, insulin sensitivity, inflammatory responses, and the circadian rhythm regulation. Interventions like time-restricted eating have shown potential in improving cardiometabolic parameters and in cancer models. However, research on the association between chrono-nutrition and chronic respiratory disease is limited, and existing evidence across different populations and conditions exhibits heterogeneity. This paper aims to provide a new perspective for understanding the role of chrono-nutrition in the prevention and control of four major chronic non-communicable diseases, suggest the focus for future research, and provide a theoretical basis for developing more personalized strategies for the prevention and management of chronic and non-communicable diseases.
papers.journal: Zhonghua liu xing bing xue za zhi = Zhonghua liuxingbingxue zazhi

papers.title: Effect of perioperative opioid-sparing multimodal analgesia on early postoperative sleep disturbance in adults undergoing elective non-cardiac, non-obstetric surgery under general anaesthesia: protocol for a systematic review and meta-analysis.
Temporal and bidirectional associations of sleep-wake behavior in adolescentes.
papers.abstract: This study investigated the temporal and bidirectional associations between wake behaviors - sedentary behavior (SB), light physical activity (LPA), and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) - and sleep patterns, including total sleep time (TST), wake after sleep onset (WASO), sleep efficiency (SE), sleep fragmentation (SF), time to bed (TTB), and time out of bed (TOB). A total of 178 adolescents (aged 15-18 years, 50.56% boys) were assessed using accelerometry over 24 hours for seven consecutive days. Multilevel linear models with random intercept were used for longitudinal analysis of bidirectional and temporal associations, adjusted for sex, age, body mass index, socioeconomic level, and day of the week. At the between-subject level, higher SB, LPA and MVPA were associated with lower TST, while higher LPA was associated with higher TTB. Higher TST was associated with lower SB, and higher TTB was associated with higher SB. At the within subject level, higher SB and LPA were associated with lower TST and WASO, and higher TST, TTB and TOB were associated with lower SB. A consistent routine for going to bed and getting up at appropriate times can enhance the availability of time for PA by reducing the time involved in SB.

papers.title: Sleep Characteristics of Elite Female Soccer Players Competing in the National Women's Soccer League Across a Competitive Season.
papers.abstract: Sleep supports recovery and readiness in professional sport, yet season-long objective data in women's professional soccer are limited. This study aimed to provide a longitudinal, objective description of sleep across a competitive season and to compare sleep characteristics between preseason and in-season phases. Twenty-seven professional athletes were monitored from January to November 2024 using a finger-worn wearable. Nightly total sleep time (TST), sleep efficiency, sleep onset latency (SOL), and sleep stage durations were extracted. Preseason versus in-season differences were examined using linear mixed-effects models and reported as estimated marginal mean differences with 95% CIs. During the in-season, TST averaged 7.8 (1.2) hours (median: 7.9 h), sleep efficiency 89.1% (5.4%), and SOL 15.6 (12.6) minutes. Mean sleep stage durations were 262.8 (52.8) minutes (light), 96.6 (31.8) minutes (deep), and 106.8 (34.2) minutes (Rapid Eye Movement). Notable night-to-night variability was observed, particularly for TST (within-player coefficients of variation: 10%-18%) and SOL (50%-114%). Compared with preseason, in-season sleep was characterized by lower REM sleep (-4.8 min, 95% CI -6.9 to -2.8; P < .001), reduced sleep efficiency (-0.37%, 95% CI -0.71 to -0.02; P = .036), and shorter SOL (-1.1 min, 95% CI -2.0 to -0.2; P = .020). TST did not differ between phases (P = .287), and deep and light sleep remained unchanged. Effect sizes were small (Cohen d ≤ 0.15). Group averages of sleep parameters might mask individual and seasonal changes in sleep, highlighting the need for longitudinal, athlete-specific monitoring to guide proactive sleep monitoring strategies.
papers.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance

papers.title: Association of Social Activity With the Timing of Objectively Measured Daily Steps in Community-Dwelling Older Adults.
papers.abstract: Afternoon and evening inactivity is common in older adults, but whether habitual social activity is associated with time-specific daily steps is unclear. We explored whether habitual social activity was associated with the timing of daily steps among community-dwelling older adults. This exploratory observational study included 2578 participants from a community-based cohort. Habitual social activity was assessed using the social domain of the Lifestyle Activities Questionnaire and was analyzed as both a total domain score and individual social activity items. Steps were objectively measured using a waist-worn accelerometer and summarized within 8 predefined 3-hour time-of-day windows. Associations were examined using function-on-scalar regression. Higher social activity was associated with more steps from 9:00 to 24:00, with estimates increasing toward the evening. Associations varied across specific activities. Among participants with lower baseline activity, multiple social activity items were positively associated with step counts mainly from morning through early evening. In this exploratory analysis, higher habitual social activity was associated with small time-specific differences in step counts from 9:00 to 24:00, with larger differences toward the evening. The stronger association among participants with lower baseline activity and heterogeneity across specific activities highlights the need to better characterize the context and timing of social activities.

papers.title: Sleeping in Extreme Conditions: A Case Study of a 2024 Vendée Globe Skipper.
papers.abstract: This case study measured the 2024 Vendée Globe winner's sleep, examined the influence of contextual factors on sleep, and described the perceived relationship between sleep and performance. Sleep was measured onshore using actigraphy and at sea using a dedicated onboard sleep-monitoring tool. Each sleep episode was manually initiated and terminated by the skipper via a computer, followed by a self-rated sleep quality score. Wind force/angle, boat speed, and air temperature were collected. A semistructured interview was conducted postrace. Over 64 days, 19 hours, 22 minutes, and 49 seconds, the skipper adopted a polyphasic sleep pattern (41.3 [10.5] episodes/24 h) characterized by a mix of independent sleep opportunities and clustered sleep attempts separated by microawakenings. Average time in bed (8h22 [2h20]) and total sleep time (6h30 [1h55]) per day were comparable to onshore values (8:03 [0:31], 6:23 [0:25]). Forty-nine percent of episodes were rated moderate to good. Nighttime episodes (9:00 PM-6:00 AM) were overrepresented, suggesting circadian rhythm preservation. Interview data identified 5 functional-impairment moments and 2 peak-functioning periods, which temporally coincided with decreasing and increasing 24-hour rolling sleep, respectively. Wind angle modestly influenced sleep duration. Despite extreme constraints of solo ocean racing, proactive in-race sleep management allowed the skipper to maintain his habitual sleep quantity/quality close to onshore baseline levels. A temporal coincidence appears to exist between operational functioning, fluctuations in 24-hour rolling sleep, and in-race major difficulties. Findings suggest that in-race "opportunistic sleep accumulation" strategies may improve performance and safety in solo offshore racing.
papers.journal: International journal of sports physiology and performance

papers.title: Brain NaV1.5 fine-tunes neuronal excitability to facilitate female-directed social behavior in male mice.
papers.abstract: The voltage-gated sodium channel NaV1.5, an essential subtype for cardiac action potential generation, is also enriched in limbic regions of the brain, but its function in the central nervous system remains poorly understood. We performed RNAscope, immunostaining, electrophysiology, fiber photometry, Scn5a knockdown, and behavioral testing to dissect the functional role of NaV1.5 in the brain. NaV1.5 channels are enriched in neurons of posterior bed nucleus of the stria terminalis (BNSTp) and accumulated at the axon initial segment. Activation of these tetrodotoxin-resistant channels lowers action potential threshold and accelerates spike initiation at relatively hyperpolarized levels of membrane potential (Vm). In vivo fiber photometry showed that BNSTp NaV1.5-expressing neurons in male mice were recruited by salient social stimuli and exhibited hyperpolarizing Vm dynamics during social contacts. Scn5a knockdown selectively attenuated neuronal responses to female chemosensory cues, and disrupted sex preference and female-directed behaviors. These findings identify NaV1.5 as a Vm state-dependent regulator of BNSTp neuronal excitability, and reveal an unexpected role of this channel subtype in female-cue processing and female-directed social behavior in males.

papers.title: Statistical Learning of Feature-Spatial Mappings and Its Modulation by Cue-Induced Expectation.
papers.abstract: Visual statistical learning enables individuals to extract regularities from the environment, thereby optimizing attentional allocation. Previous research has mainly focused on unidimensional location or feature probability learning, leaving unclear whether individuals can acquire multidimensional mappings between target features and high-probability spatial locations, and how cue-induced expectations modulate the neural expression of such mappings. We employed a location probability paradigm combined with multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA) and recorded EEG. Reaction times showed a significant gradient from the feature-matched high-probability location to the low-probability location, indicating successful acquisition of feature-spatial mappings under both cue conditions. The N2pc did not reliably differentiate the two high-probability location conditions, providing no detectable evidence of feature-dependent modulation of early lateralized selection. Predictive cues elicited brief pretarget alpha lateralization toward the cue-associated HPTL. Search-array-locked MVPA discriminated feature-matched from feature-mismatched HPTL trials under both cue conditions, with stronger decoding under predictive cueing. These findings show that learned feature-spatial regularities were expressed behaviorally and in distributed neural activity, and that predictive cues modulated their neural expression before and after search-array onset.

papers.title: From Polycystic Ovary Syndrome to Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome: A Practical Clinical Review.
papers.abstract: Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS), recently renamed Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS), is the most common endocrine disorder affecting women of reproductive age. The new nomenclature reflects growing recognition that this condition extends far beyond ovarian dysfunction, encompassing complex endocrine, metabolic, cardiovascular, and psychological abnormalities. Although the diagnostic criteria remain unchanged, the name change emphasizes the multisystem nature of the disorder and may improve disease recognition and patient care. This review provides a practical, evidence-based overview of the diagnosis and management of PMOS/PCOS, highlighting recent updates from the 2023 International Evidence-Based Guideline. We discuss the evaluation of hyperandrogenism and ovulatory dysfunction in reproductive-aged women, as well as the assessment and treatment of obesity, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, dyslipidemia, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, obstructive sleep apnea, and mental health disorders. Finally, we summarize current pharmacological therapies and emerging treatment strategies, highlighting key knowledge gaps that must be bridged to optimize long-term cardiometabolic and reproductive outcomes.
papers.journal: The American journal of the medical sciences

papers.title: Influence of chiropractic care on sleep-related behavior of athletic Mangalarga Marchador horses.
papers.abstract: Sleep is a fundamental biological process for homeostasis in mammals. Chiropractic is a manual therapeutic approach that aims to restore joint mobility, correct biomechanical dysfunctions, and optimize welfare. The present study examined the influence of chiropractic sessions on resting behavior patterns of Mangalarga Marchador horses raised in an intensive system. Nine Mangalarga Marchador horses, with an average age of 4.2 ± 1.2 years, were evaluated for their sleep-related behavior over 72 hours, followed by a chiropractic session, and reassessed over the next 72 hours post-session. After 35 days, horses received a second chiropractic session and were observed for another 72 hours, pre- and post-session. There was a reduction in wakefulness time (Pre: 1,128.22±32.02; Post: 1,063.66±29.16 min, p=0.003) and an increase in time in lateral recumbency after the chiropractic sessions (1st: from 129.24±43.88 min to 147.14±46.25 min and 2nd: from 88.55±28.19 min to 143.10±38.58 min, p=0.004). These results suggest that chiropractic care is associated with changes in sleep-related behavior in athletic horses. Further studies using electroencephalography are needed to determine whether these behavioral changes are associated with alterations in sleep physiology.

papers.title: EEG-VTSFN: An enhanced approach for differentiating between unipolar and bipolar mood disorders.
papers.abstract: Accurate differentiation between Bipolar Disorder (BD) and Unipolar Depression (UD) is a significant clinical challenge due to overlapping manifestations and a lack of objective biomarkers. While EEG offers high temporal resolution, its psychiatric utility for diagnostic differentiation remains limited. To address this, we propose the Variational Autoencoder (VAE)-based Time-Space Fusion Network (VTSFN). VTSFN transforms complex EEG signals into latent-space representations to mitigate noise and construct stable latent co-activation patterns. By integrating Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and attention mechanisms, the model captures temporal dynamics to identify discriminative patterns. Our results demonstrate that VTSFN achieved the highest accuracy and AUC point estimates among the evaluated models, with a test-set accuracy of 79.3% (95% CI, 65.5%-93.1%) and an AUC of 82.7% (95% CI, 63.2%-98.5%), without significant paired AUC differences at p < 0.01. Validation in a diagnostic-switch (tBD) cohort (n = 22) identified 17/22 converters (sensitivity, 77.3%; 95% CI, 59.1%-90.9%), requiring further longitudinal validation. Exploratory feature analysis revealed that, compared with UD patients, BD and tBD patients exhibited weaker latent co-activation in right parieto-temporal and temporo-occipital regions, alongside stronger latent co-activation in left frontal-right parietal and temporal regions. These model-derived channel similarity patterns require independent validation.

papers.title: Co-developmental trajectories of internalizing symptoms and psychotic-like experiences among adolescents: The predictive role of sleep disturbance.
papers.abstract: Internalizing symptoms and psychotic-like experiences (PLEs) are common among adolescents. However, few studies have explored the longitudinal co-development of internalizing symptoms and PLEs in this age group. A total of 7529 adolescents (M age at baseline = 13.89 years, SD = 1.34; 50% girls) participated in this three-wave longitudinal study. A parallel-process latent class growth analysis identified joint trajectories of internalizing symptoms and PLEs, and multinomial logistic regression examined the effect of sleep disturbance. Three distinct trajectories were identified: a low-risk group (74.0%), a pure-internalizing symptoms group (13.5%), and a chronic co-occurring group (12.5%). After controlling for sample characteristics, negative life events during follow-up, and sleep duration, baseline sleep disturbance was significantly associated with both the pure-internalizing symptoms trajectory (OR = 3.41, 95% CI = 2.84-4.08) and the chronic co-occurring trajectory (OR = 3.69, 95% CI = 3.06-4.46). These findings indicate that sleep disturbance independently associated with the heterogeneous co-developmental trajectories of internalizing symptoms and PLEs. Early assessment and treatment of sleep disturbance may be an important strategy for the prevention and intervention of psychopathology development.

papers.title: Towards semantic brain-computer interfacing: The graded inventory of semantic triggers (GIST) paradigm.
papers.abstract: Semantic Brain-Computer Interfaces (sBCIs) aim to decode conceptual information directly from neural activity, enabling more efficient and natural communication for individuals with severe motor impairments. However, existing approaches are often confounded by stimulus-driven perceptual processes and lack a reliable means of tagging the moment of concept formation. We introduce the Graded Inventory of Semantic Triggers (GIST), a novel electroencephalography (EEG) paradigm designed to elicit semantic retrieval from graded verbal clues with precise temporal alignment.Approach: EEG data were recorded from 14 participants performing the GIST task across three semantic categories (food, musical instruments, and body parts). Target neural activity was aligned to each participant's self-reported moment of semantic retrieval (spacebar press), enabling response-locked analysis. Here, we propose a staged framework where the first comprises a Conformer-based encoder trained on pooled data using a hybrid contrastive objective that combines instance-level consistency and cross-participant class alignment with domain-adversarial learning to reduce participant-specific information. In the second stage, the frozen encoder is transferred to a held-out participant whose data played no part in Stage 1, and a support vector machine is calibrated on that participant's own labelled items under a nested leave-one-item-out protocol.Results: Above-chance semantic decoding was achieved in all three pairwise tasks. Mean accuracies were 73.4% (Body vs. Food), 70.7% (Body vs. Music), and 68.2% (Food vs. Music). Participant-level permutation tests were significant in 9/11 participants for Body vs. Food and 8/11 for each of the other tasks (p < 0.05). The pre-response interval at [-1.5s, -0.5s] was the most discriminative.Significance: The GIST paradigm enables controlled elicitation and temporal alignment of semantic processing while reducing perceptual confounds. Combined with cross-participant representation pretraining and participant-specific calibration, the results demonstrate above-chance decoding of semantic categories from EEG in individuals excluded from representation learning, supporting the feasibility of sBCIs.

papers.title: ACF-Net: Design of an adaptive cross-modal fusion network for cross-subject wearable EEG-EMG gesture recognition.
papers.abstract: Cross-subject gesture recognition in wearable brain-computer interfaces is constrained by four structural deficiencies: symmetric cross-modal attention discarding cortical precedence over muscular execution, priors confined to post hoc analysis, invariance anchored on unimodal features, and adaptation requiring labelled target-domain data. This study closes these gaps by embedding corticomuscular coupling directly into the network architecture rather than recovering it from data.Approach: ACF-Net is a four-stage pipeline embedding neurophysiological priors directly into fusion. The corticomuscular coherence prior injection layer (CMC-Prior) encodes time-lagged coherence and phase-locking values for every electroencephalography (EEG)-electromyography (EMG) channel pair as a learnable bias tensor. Granger-causality-inspired directed cross-modal attention (GC-Attn) uses a causal mask allowing only EEG-to-EMG influence within 30-120 ms. The fused embedding is projected onto a symmetric positive definite manifold with log-Euclidean triplet loss. Physiology-consistent test-time adaptation (PC-TTA) updates only batch-normalisation affine parameters, using EEG-precedes-EMG as unlabelled self-supervision, eliminating labelled target data. Leave-one-subject-out validation on WAY-EEG-GAL (12 participants) and WEE-Ges (20 participants, three days) used fold-wise priors and Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests.Main results: ACF-Net reached 87.6% on WAY-EEG-GAL and 89.2% on WEE-Ges, exceeding the strongest baseline by 9.4 and 9.1 percentage points with all comparisons significant after correction. Ablation attributed gains of 6.3, 4.9, 3.4 and 1.8 percentage points to directed attention, prior injection, manifold embedding and test-time adaptation. Accuracy remained 77.5% under 20 mm simulated electrode displacement, adaptation reduced the cross-day loss from 6.8 to 2.1 percentage points, and a forward pass on an NVIDIA Jetson Nano took 32.4 ms within a 178 ms end-to-end response at 30.9 Hz. Significance: Learned coupling weights recovered central-to-forearm-extensor projection, and delays matched corticospinal conduction with motor-unit recruitment, suggesting physiological structure, not dataset-specific statistics. Yet healthy young adults, gel-based/semi-dry wired hardware, and simulated displacement make this methodological; clinical and wireless dry-electrode transfer remains unestablished.

papers.title: Exploratory heart rate variability patterns across sleep stages following a 7-day multicomponent mantra-based cognitive intervention: A pilot randomized pre-post controlled study.
papers.abstract: Cognitive-contemplative practices could potentially affect autonomic function, but existing research has focused on waking measures of heart rate variability (HRV). It remains unclear whether changes associated with brief interventions differ across sleep stages. To determine whether differences in HRV according to sleep stage would differ in a group undergoing a 7-day, multicomponent, Hare Krishna mantra-based cognitive therapy (HMBCT) intervention compared to a group engaging in their normal routine activities. Thirty-four healthy males aged 18-30 years were randomized to HMBCT (n = 17) or a usual-routine control condition (n = 17). Overnight polysomnography with continuous ECG was conducted at baseline and after the 7-day intervention period. HRV variables were calculated using time-domain and Poincaré/geometric HRV indices separately for REM, N2, and N3 sleep stages. Group × Time interactions were analyzed using repeated measures ANOVA, and then subjected to Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (FDR) correction in 30 primary tests. Nine interactions reached the nominal uncorrected threshold (p < .05): four in REM (SDNN, RMSSD, SD1, SD2) and five in N2 (SDNN, RMSSD, pNN50, SD1, CVI), while none did so in N3. Effect sizes of REM/N2 interaction were estimated as partial η2p = 0.120-0.173. However, none remained statistically significant after FDR correction (smallest q = 0.148). Nominal interactions were more pronounced in REM and N2 sleep stages, but none of the primary interactions survived multiple testing correction. Thus the results are exploratory and should be confirmed in other studies.

papers.title: Morning lighting intervention reduces fatigue and improves sleep in Parkinson disease.
papers.abstract: Fatigue and sleep disturbances are common in Parkinson Disease (PD) and significantly reduce quality of life, yet effective pharmacological treatments are limited. Light therapy offers a promising non-pharmacologic approach, but most lighting interventions have focused on improving sleep. Using a novel and easily administered morning lighting intervention, we previously demonstrated improvement in sleep duration. We have now extended the prior study through the addition of 23 individuals to investigate the intervention's effect on fatigue and sleep. In this single-arm intervention study, participants received morning light for 4 consecutive weeks from table or floor luminaires designed to deliver circadian-effective ambient light at home. Objective sleep was measured with wrist-worn actigraphy and subjective sleep, fatigue and mood were assessed using standardized questionnaires. Analysis of pre and post intervention data for the current cohort was performed separately as well as in combination with the 20 participants from the previously reported pilot study. For the 23 current participants, fatigue on the Functional Assessment of Chronic Illness Therapy-Fatigue (FACIT-F) scale improved by 3.9 ± 1.00 points (p = 0.0026). While sleep duration increased by mean 21.3 ± 14.4 min, it was not statistically significant (p = 0.082). When combined with the 20 participants from the prior pilot study, significant improvement in fatigue by 2.8 ± 0.85 points (p = 0.0033) was observed and sleep duration was also significantly increased by 24.7 ± 10.4 min (p = 0.012). These findings support morning light as a novel intervention for fatigue in PD.
papers.journal: Neurotherapeutics : the journal of the American Society for Experimental NeuroTherapeutics

papers.title: A fungal clock protein exerts extra-circadian roles in nitrogen metabolism and mitochondrial function.
papers.abstract: Protein moonlighting refers to functions in polypeptides exceeding those considered canonical roles. While this vision is changing our understanding of cellular signaling integration, in timekeeping proteins this duality, if any, remains mostly unexplored. Circadian clocks are widespread cellular machineries that converge on shared architectural principles, built around negative feedback loops involving the activity of pacemaker proteins. In fungi, FREQUENCY (FRQ) is the defining timeteller, but whether it has roles outside the clock is unknown. Here, we show that the FRQ protein of the fungal phytopathogen Botrytis cinerea also operates as a clock-independent metabolic hub. Loss of FRQ results in the inability to release Nitrogen Catabolite Repression, while the loss-of-function mutant accumulates elevated reactive oxygen species and exhibits sensitivity to mitochondria-targeting fungicides. Secondary metabolite profiles are also largely altered. Together, our findings establish that a core clock protein moonlights as a metabolic integrator, independent of its clock function, raising the question of whether metabolic scaffolding represents an underappreciated role of circadian pacemaker proteins.

papers.title: When brain networks crash: connectivity, slow-wave activity and neural replay in Alzheimer's disease.
papers.abstract: Brain connectivity disruption is a hallmark of neurodegenerative disorders, including Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet how network breakdown gives rise to cognitive deficits remains unclear. Here, we review the evidence bearing on three interconnected processes that have been proposed to link molecular pathology to cognitive decline. First, we summarize evidence that misfolded proteins propagate along brain connectivity pathways, making the connectome the biological substrate for disease progression. Second, we discuss the divergent trajectory reported across the AD continuum, an initial compensatory hyperconnectivity followed by progressive hypoconnectivity and network collapse, together with the accompanying oscillatory changes (intrusion of slow-wave activity and suppression of fast oscillatory rhythms). Third, we examine the proposal that these oscillatory alterations compromise neural replay mechanisms, critical for memory consolidation, representing the potential link between network dysfunction and cognitive decline. By integrating evidence from human neuroimaging, electrophysiology, and animal models in the AD field, this framework offers new perspectives for therapeutic interventions targeting brain connectivity and replay mechanisms in neurodegenerative diseases.

papers.title: Characteristics of Women Ages 40-60 with Menopausal Symptoms: United States, 2025.
papers.abstract: The menopausal transition is a critical window for the health of women and may serve as an inflection point for the onset of chronic disease. During this transition, a woman's ovaries become less efficient at producing estrogen and progesterone, and women may experience symptoms such as hot flashes, night sweats, insomnia or sleep disturbances, and abnormal uterine bleeding. This report describes demographic and geographic characteristics of women ages 40-60 who had menopausal symptoms in the past 12 months using data from the 2025 National Health Interview Survey (NHIS). Estimates of current prescription medication use for menopausal symptoms by age are also provided. NHIS is a nationally representative household survey of the civilian, non-institutionalized U.S. population. Point estimates and the corresponding confidence intervals for this analysis were calculated using SAS-callable SUDAAN software to account for the complex sample design of NHIS. In 2025, nearly one in two women (49.4%) ages 40-60 who were not currently pregnant, postpartum, or in surgical menopause reported menopausal symptoms in the past 12 months. The presence of symptoms varied by age, race and ethnicity, educational attainment, and urbanization level. Women ages 48-51 (62.0%) and 52-55 (67.4%) were the most likely to report menopausal symptoms compared with younger and older women. Among women who reported menopausal symptoms in the past 12 months, 15.6% indicated that they were currently taking a prescription medication for those symptoms. Of these women, prescription use was highest among women ages 52-55 and 56-60.

papers.title: Restless legs syndrome and other neurological disorders: A systematic-narrative hybrid literature review with exploratory meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a sleep-related sensorimotor disorder affecting approximately 3% of adults worldwide. This review aims to synthesize current evidence on associations between RLS and major neurological conditions, provide an exploratory quantitative synthesis summarizing association patterns and heterogeneity, and identify priority mechanistic and clinical research gaps. Databases were searched from inception until August 2026. In our exploratory synthesis of 119 unique studies, RLS was significantly associated with Parkinson's disease (case-control OR 3.22, 95% CI 2.35-4.41; cohort RR 1.74, 95% CI 1.02-2.95), multiple sclerosis (OR 4.04, 95% CI 3.26-5.00), neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder (OR 2.91, 95% CI 1.45-5.84), migraine or headache disorders (forward OR 2.72, 95% CI 2.19-3.38; reverse adjusted OR 1.53, 95% CI 1.36-1.73), peripheral neuropathy (OR 3.82, 95% CI 2.49-5.83), epilepsy (OR 2.11, 95% CI 1.58-2.82), and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (OR 7.69, 95% CI 2.74-21.59). This work is an evidence-mapping review with exploratory pooling and is not intended as a definitive evidence synthesis. RLS is likely associated with neurodegenerative and other specific neurological conditions. Recognition of these associations may support earlier identification of comorbid conditions and targeted management strategies. However, the current evidence remains observational and heterogeneous.

papers.title: Delayed school start-times and adolescent sleep duration: A systematic umbrella review.
papers.abstract: Expert panels have long recommended delayed school start-times (SSTs) as necessary for addressing widespread adolescent sleep loss; nevertheless, adoption of recommendations has been slow. The major goals of this umbrella review were to explore the consistency of review teams' recommendations while describing and assessing review quality. We used systematic procedures to identify five meta-analyses and four narrative reviews. Authors of all nine reviews concluded that adolescent sleep duration (ASD) likely increased when SSTs were later but usually recommended limited adoption. Reviewers' hesitancy to recommend widespread adoption reflected (a) the modest average sleep gains reported in two reviews that met all AMSTAR2 critical criteria for producing sound estimates of effectiveness, (b) the lack of evidence that gains in sleep were sustained, and (c) the limited quality of primary studies. Potential moderating factors (e.g., students' background, school type and size) were explored but little progress was made due to missing data; however geographic location was identified as a potential moderator of SSTs' impact on ASD. Our results support the need for well-controlled local studies of SST delays that are guided by standard reporting protocols. We also recommend needs assessments to capture local sleep norms and unique community conditions. Registration: PROSPERO CRD42023373423.

papers.title: Predictors of residual obstructive sleep apnea after mandibular distraction osteogenesis in infants with Pierre Robin sequence: Insight on syndromic stratification.
papers.abstract: Mandibular distraction osteogenesis (MDO) improves obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in infants with Pierre Robin sequence (PRS), but residual disease is common. We sought to identify predictors of residual severe OSA after MDO. We performed a retrospective cohort study of infants with PRS who underwent MDO and postoperative polysomnography (PSG) at a tertiary pediatric center between 2019 and 2025. Residual severe OSA was defined a priori as postoperative obstructive apnea-hypopnea index (oAHI) > 10 events/hour or postoperative need for a tracheostomy. Candidate predictors were evaluated using univariate logistic regression. Stickler syndrome was analyzed both within and excluded from the syndromic category based on its tongue-base airway physiology resembling isolated PRS. Thirty-three infants met inclusion criteria, of whom 11 (33.3%) had residual severe OSA; one required tracheostomy. Syndromic diagnosis excluding Stickler syndrome (odds ratio [OR] 5.95, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.22-28.95, p = 0.03), neurologic hypotonia (OR = 5.40, 95%CI 1.08-26.93, p = 0.04) and higher preoperative oAHI (OR = 1.04 per event/hour, 95%CI 1.01-1.07, p = 0.02) were associated with residual severe OSA. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic analysis demonstrated modest discrimination (AUC = 0.70, 95%CI 0.43-0.97) with an optimal preoperative oAHI cutoff of 96 events/hour (50% sensitivity, 95% specificity). Among 25 infants with paired PSGs, median oAHI reduction was similar between the non-syndromic/Stickler and syndromic groups (90.5% vs 87.6%, p = 0.3). One-third of infants had residual severe OSA after MDO. Higher preoperative oAHI, neurologic hypotonia, and syndromic diagnosis excluding Stickler syndrome were associated with residual disease and may help identify infants who warrant closer postoperative PSG surveillance.

papers.title: The unique contributions of negative emotionality and sleep problems to toddlers' physiological stress response.
papers.abstract: Previous research has examined temperament and sleep separately with respect to their relationship to young children's physiological stress response; however, little research has jointly investigated these two constructs in relation to children's physiological stress response. Previous research also has not considered the potential contributions of individual components of children's negative emotionality to their stress response. In the present study, mothers reported on children's negative emotionality and sleep problems when children were 18 and 24 months old respectively. When children were 30 months old, saliva samples were collected prior to and after the stranger approach task to assess physiological stress response as measured by total cortisol secretion (AUCg) and cortisol reactivity (AUCi). Results showed that frustration was positively associated with AUCg. Frustration and sleep problems were also both positively associated with AUCi, and shyness was negatively associated with AUCi. No other dimensions of negative emotionality were related to AUCg or AUCi. These results highlight the unique contributions of toddlers' temperament and sleep difficulties to their stress physiology. Furthermore, these results highlight the importance of parsing out the individual components of negative emotionality when conducting temperament research on children's stress response.

papers.title: Sleep in the first three years of life: Age-related patterns and predictors in a South African sample.
papers.abstract: Sleep is integral to early neurodevelopment and health, yet most normative data derive from high-income, global North populations. Context-specific data from sub-Saharan Africa, and South Africa in particular, remain scarce.
